title: Democrats launch Nvidia investigation, write scathing letter on Huang’s ‘scheme’ with Trump
lede: Rep. Richard Neal and Sen. Ron Wyden opened an inquiry into how the Trump administration handled Nvidia chip sales to China, aimed at Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick as much as at Nvidia.

points: Their letter asks Commerce to preserve records on an H200 export arrangement they call illegal.
It alleges Taiwan-made chips were routed through the U.S. so a tariff could take a cut, in effect an unconstitutional export tax.
It asks why Megaspeed kept buying chips after intelligence about Alice Huang and her ties to Jensen Huang reached Lutnick.
It notes the export deal followed $26 million in Nvidia donations to Trump projects, including the ballroom.
As the minority they cannot compel answers; a separate Republican-led probe has secured Huang's agreement to testify.

sections.text: The inquiry goes after the export licences that let advanced Nvidia GPUs reach China, the same rules that shape how AI compute is supplied worldwide.
